claims.text:
Sakalthôr is an Adûnaic name. Its meaning is not glossed, but Paul Strack suggests it means "Shore-son" and is a compound of sakal ("shore") and the suffix -thôr ("-son"). The meaning of the Adûnaic prefix Ar- is not glossed, but Paul Strack suggests it means "king" and is a prefixal form of ârû ("king") or derived from the same root.
Falassion is a Quenya name. Its meaning is not glossed, but Paul Strack suggests it means "Shore-son" and is a compound of falassë ("shore") and the patronymic suffix -ion ("-son"). Like for all the rulers of Númenor whose name was inscribed in the Scroll of Kings, the prefix tar- ("high") was added to his name.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "The Line of Elros: Kings of Númenor", first paragraph and entry I to XXV
